title: AI Bond Issuance Freezes in September at Just $23 Billion; Morgan Stanley: Hyperscale Cloud Providers to Return to Market in Q4
source_used: BigGo Finance (relaying a Morgan Stanley research report)
key_facts: Morgan Stanley data: global AI-related bond issuance fell to about $23 billion in September 2026, the second-lowest month this year, and US investment-grade AI issuance was zero
Year-to-date AI bond issuance reached $466 billion by end-September, more than double 2025's full-year $216 billion; June was the peak at $113 billion
Google, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft issued about $132 billion of investment-grade bonds this year; with Oracle and SpaceX the six raised about $254 billion

Morgan Stanley calls September "a pause, not a retreat", blaming front-loaded issuance, permitting, power and political obstacles to data centres, and rising rates; it expects issuance to recover in Q4
Non-dollar issuance by hyperscalers is about $72 billion this year; Amazon sold a 4.25 billion pound bond in September; SoftBank sold about $10 billion of high-yield bonds
Morgan Stanley estimates the six hyperscalers' 2027 capital spending at about $1.4 trillion, above the market consensus of $1 to 1.1 trillion
quote_evidence: Morgan Stanley, in its latest report, characterized the slowdown as "a pause, not a retreat," and expects issuance momentum to gradually recover in the fourth quarter

According to Morgan Stanley's data, cumulative global AI-related bond issuance reached $466 billion (approximately NT$14.8 trillion) through the end of September, more than double last year's full-year total of $216 billion
why_it_matters_hint: The AI debt machine paused in September, but the bank expects it to restart with even bigger 2027 spending plans
notes: BigGo Finance is a Taiwan-based finance news site; the figures are Morgan Stanley's, not independently checked. Likely translated from a Chinese-language original.
